task: Several regional governors have raised private armies under the pretext of local defence, and their forces now collectively outnumber the standing national army. The central government's tax collectors and judicial officers are being turned away at provincial borders. One governor has begun minting coins bearing his own insignia, and another has negotiated a separate truce with a neighbouring power without central authorisation. The state risks permanent fragmentation if this trend continues unchecked. Design a strategy to restore central military authority that combines political incentives, targeted enforcement, and institutional reforms, while avoiding a multi-front civil war that the centre cannot currently win.

dispatches.responsibility: Issue the legitimating edict: amnesty terms for compliant governors, honorific incentives, and the public doctrine that all armies, coinage, and treaties belong to the centre
Dispatch envoys to each governor separately to probe intentions, split the coalition, offer negotiated compliance paths, and diplomatically address the unauthorised truce with the neighbouring power
Prepare narrowly targeted legal enforcement against the single most flagrant offender (private minting) to demonstrate resolve without provoking a general revolt
Design the institutional reforms: recentralisation of tax collection, unified military command and officer rotation, and fiscal guarantees that make continued loyalty more profitable than secession
